newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on Cargill, local buying.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on Cargill, local buying.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on day-long Cargill demand and a closing local short covering rally.
"Cargill bought 750 July contracts through the day. Locals were the main sellers, then they had a short covering rally at the close," a trader said.
May WCE futures crush profit margin fell to -14.59 Tuesday from -13.65 Monday. About 500 July-Nov spread at $47.50, 500 May-Nov $43. Volume was 8,420 lots.
Japan bought 1,000 tonnes canola overnight, sources said.
May canola rose $4.40 to $421.10, July closed up $4.70 at $426.10 and November ended up $4.30 at $378.50. May flax lost $0.50 as commercials sold 100 May-July at $2.50. Volume was 400 lots.

May western barley fell $1.40 to $140.10 and July settled $0.90 lower at $139.60 with the Pools selling to UGG, traders said. Locals were light sellers. About 200 May-July spread from $0.80 to $0.50 sold by Benson Quinn and Alberta Wheat Pool, traders said. Volume 1,200.
May feed wheat slipped $0.40 to close at $171.90 and July fell $0.70 to $168.90. Alberta Wheat Pool was the best seller, a trader said. May-July was bid at $3, offered at $3.50. Volume 500 lots.
Oats and feed peas did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except feed peas and oats)
